HEADER

Menu open — desktop 1280, actual size

shared chrome, every public page · unmodified

This is fine. The header's keyboard and screen-reader wiring is already correct — aria-expanded on the trigger, Escape closes from anywhere, an outside click dismisses, focus returns to the trigger, and the closed menu is visibility:hidden so its 20 links are not in the tab order.

HEADER FIXMED

Landscape phone — the menu collapses to a sliver

At 844×390 the menu is 70 px tall and holds 700 px of content — 10.6x its own height. Twenty links in a sliver. Both panels are 1:1 at 844×390.

before — 70px of menu
after — anchored to the header
why / the code

The menu is max-height:calc(100vh - 320px), and the mobile override that repositions it is gated on @media(max-width:767px). So any window wider than 767 but short falls back to the desktop rule — a landscape phone, or a short desktop window. Measured across nine viewports:

Viewportmenucontentverdict
390×844 portrait358×5361028pxscrolls, usable
1280×900 desktop760×403399pxfits
844×390 landscape588×70700 pxunusable

Also 100vh, not 100dvh — the exact unit defect index.tsx already fixed for .home-shell, still present in the shared chrome. And 320 corresponds to nothing nameable, which is the same magic-number family as the 108/96 header heights.

/* anchor to the header, and use dvh: 140 = the 108px header + 32px of air */
.nav-menu{max-height:calc(100dvh - 140px)}
CHANGES

Three repairs — one line each

A  The word is missing entirely without JavaScript, and for ~200ms on every single load.

before — no word
after
why / the code

cycleW starts null, so the first render writes no inline width. .home-cycle is overflow:hidden and all four words are position:absolute, so they add nothing to its intrinsic width — it computes to 0px and clips the word away. Measured on a normal load, JS working, local server, no network: 4 painted frames, ~200ms.

.home-cycle{width:max-content}   /* resting width, needs no JS */
.home-cyc-word.on{
  position:static;      /* the visible word sits in flow, so the pill has a width */
  display:inline-block; /* NOT optional - see below */
}

display:inline-block is load-bearing, and measuring this mock is what caught it. position:static alone makes the span a non-replaced inline box, whose offsetWidth is 0 — so the existing effect would write width:0px over max-content and the pill would collapse on every load with JavaScript, turning a 200ms flash into a permanent one.

B  Resize with reduced motion on and the word stays cut — 96 px, 35% of it — for good.

before — cut off
after
why / the code

Width is measured in an effect keyed on the word index alone; there is no resize listener. The font is clamp(36px,4.3vw,60px), so width is a function of viewport width. On a normal load a stale value self-heals at the next 2400ms tick; under reduced motion the interval never starts, so it is final. Reproduced here by writing the 182 px width measured at 390 onto a 1280 frame, where the word needs 278 px.

const ro = new ResizeObserver( measure );   // not window.resize: this also
if ( markRef.current ) ro.observe( markRef.current );  // catches a webfont swap
return () => ro.disconnect();

C  Reduced motion can park a white shutter over the tint — latent today, one edit away from live.

before — white pill
after
why / the code

The reduced-motion block sets the shutter to scaleX(1) — the start state — under a comment saying it settles the pill into its resting state, which is scaleX(0). The dot's sibling rule is correct, so it is a slip. It is overridden today only because .home-layout.show .home-mark::before scores (0,2,1) against this rule's (0,1,1).

@media(prefers-reduced-motion:reduce){
  .home-mark::before{transform:scaleX(0)}   /* was scaleX(1) */
}
DHIGH

WCAG 1.4.12 fails — user text spacing cuts 22% of the word

1.4.12 is Level AA and normative: a reader's own stylesheet setting line-height 1.5, letter-spacing .12em and word-spacing .16em must not clip anything. The word needs 356.8px; the pill stays at 278px. Both panels have those overrides applied.

before — 22% cut
after
why / the code

Same root cause as A and B from a third angle: a JavaScript-measured width on an overflow:hidden box cannot survive anything that changes glyph metrics. Fixes A + B close this — max-content is right under any spacing, and the ResizeObserver refires when the word's box changes. No extra code. It promotes those two from “repairs a flash” to “clears an AA failure”.

EHIGH

Translating the page clips the word by 39px

Not hypothetical — the site ships a language switcher, and the whole site-language service exists to translate this page. A translation rewrites the text and nothing else, so the pill keeps the width measured for English: “consumers” 278px, “उपभोक्ताओं” needs 317px.

before — clipped
after
why / the code

Devanagari is also taller than Latin at the same size, so the clipping is not only horizontal. Fixes A + B close this too, for the same reason as D.

FHIGH

Foldables — the menu reaches zero height

The menu failure needs a viewport that is wide and short — rare on a phone or laptop, and the normal shape of a folded-landscape device. All six panels are 1:1 at real foldable viewports. 844×390 was the mild case.

Galaxy Fold, folded, landscape — 653×280. Computed max-height is 0px; the 32px left is padding and border, holding 20 links and 1028px of content.

before — 0px of menu
after

Z Fold 5 cover, landscape — 882×344. 24px.

before — 24px
after

Z Flip 5, landscape — 880×360. 40px. Z Flip and Z Fold are the two best-selling foldables, so this is not an exotic posture.

before — 40px
after
why / the code — and a gap in my first fix

My earlier fix would not have worked. I replaced only the desktop calc(100vh - 320px). At 653px wide the mobile override applies instead — calc(100vh - 308px) — and 308 exceeds a 280px viewport, so it resolves negative and clamps to zero. Both rules have to change:

/* 140 = the 108px header + 32px of air. dvh for mobile browser chrome. */
.nav-menu{max-height:calc(100dvh - 140px)}
@media(max-width:767px){ .nav-menu{max-height:calc(100dvh - 140px)} }

Resulting heights: 280 → 140px, 344 → 204px, 360 → 220px, 390 → 250px.

The reasoning already exists in this repo. src/styles/Layout.css:2185 and :2204 handle exactly this for the dashboard's bottom nav, with a comment naming the trap — “an unfolded inner display is tablet-WIDE but often phone-TALL … short and wide (a landscape fold…)” — plus vertical-viewport-segments: 2 as the real posture signal, asserted by BottomNav.test.tsx:140. The dashboard learned it; the public chrome never did. Note that rule carries a max-width:768px ceiling which would not cover the 880 and 882 cases, so the header needs the height condition without it.

GMED

Foldables — the band's own sentence falls below the fold

This band exists to say what the page is about, and on two folded-landscape postures the sentence does not fit: it ends at 314px on a 280px viewport and 359px on a 344px one. Both 1:1 — scroll is disabled in the panels, so what you see is what fits.

Galaxy Fold folded landscape 653×280
Z Fold 5 cover landscape 882×344
why

Every other posture in the sixteen measured fits. A 280px-tall viewport is genuinely hostile, so this is a judgement rather than a defect — but it interacts with the 80px of blank above the headline that is already an open question: on these two postures, that padding is the difference.

Clean across all sixteen, and worth recording so it is not re-checked: zero horizontal overflow, and the pill never crosses the viewport edge — including at 280px, narrower than the 320px floor animcheck tests.

HMED

Brand lockup font — the one type change you approved

The WECARE.DIGITAL lockup declares no font of its own. It inherits body, set in src/styles/Layout.css. The hero declares its own stack at index.tsx:797. Two declarations for one typeface, and only one of them belongs to the thing it styles.

ElementResolved stack
.logo / .brand-stack — inherited Inter, ui-sans-serif, system-ui, -apple-system, "Segoe UI", Roboto, Helvetica, Arial, sans-serif
.home-head / .home-sub — declared Inter, -apple-system, BlinkMacSystemFont, "Segoe UI", Roboto, sans-serif

Faithful before / after — they are identical, and that is the point.

before — inherited stack
after — declared stack
before
after

Why it is worth doing anyway. Below, the same pair with the global stylesheet absent — one refactor, one import move. The logo drops off Inter; the headline does not, because it owns its stack. This is not hypothetical: I produced it by accident while trimming CSS out of this mock.

before — logo loses Inter
after — logo keeps Inter
why / the code — and two things I had wrong

There is no visible difference, and I am not going to imply one. I rendered “WECARE.DIGITAL” at 800/23px in both stacks, with Inter available and with fonts.googleapis.com blocked: 195.59px against 195.59px, 0px delta both times. font-feature-settings is inherited, so both get Inter's cv02/cv03/cv04/cv11 variants too — measured, not assumed. On macOS, Windows and Android both stacks land on the same system UI face.

Correction 1. I first wrote that the lockup rides on @aws-amplify/ui-react's stylesheet. It does not. The winning rule is body{font-family:Inter,…} in our own src/styles/Layout.css, with Inter first and deliberate font-feature-settings. So the exposure is smaller than I said — it is our stylesheet, not a dependency.

Correction 2, and it is a finding. index.tsx's own comment says this page rendered in Inter “only because @aws-amplify/ui-react's styles.css sets a font-family on body”. That is not true — Layout.css sets it, on purpose. The justification written into the source for the hero declaring its stack locally rests on a misattribution. The conclusion still stands; the reason given does not. That is the eleventh incorrect comment claim in this band.

/* Header.tsx - the same declaration as index.tsx:797, byte for byte */
.hdr,.logo,.brand-lockup,.brand-stack{
  font-family:'Inter',-apple-system,BlinkMacSystemFont,'Segoe UI',Roboto,sans-serif;
}

Better still: one shared token both files reference, so a third copy cannot drift. Wider than you asked for, so noted rather than done.

REST

Housekeeping, and two calls for you

No visual change, same commit: permanent will-change:width; a max-width:900px on the h1 that never binds; the h1's raw text repeating the word set five times; nine stale comments.

Your call, not mocked: the 9.6s rotation that cannot be paused, and 80 px of blank above the first word.

detail
  • will-change:width should be set shortly before a transition and released after; left on it holds compositing resources for the page's life, and under reduced motion there is no transition to hint at. Not applied in the panels — a performance judgement.
  • max-width:900px never binds: .home-hero is align-items:flex-start, so the h1 shrink-wraps to 506 px at 1280.
  • The h1's raw text — screen readers are correct, but a naive extractor reads:
    Everyday AI, built forconsumers, enterprises, climate tech, frontier techconsumersenterprisesclimate techfrontier tech
  • Comments contradict the band in nine places, two measurable: the header says climate tech is 290px with an 83px spread across five words; animcheck measures 298px and 22px across four.
  • Rotation: WCAG 2.2.2 covers content moving automatically past five seconds. Hover+focus pausing adds no furniture; a strict reading wants a user-operable control, which is furniture in a band meant to carry none.
  • The 80 px was tuned around the deleted lime brand badge. Purely cosmetic.

Deferred until this band is signed off: the other three bands, the sitewide schema problems, and propagating this band to the remaining public pages.
